source_title: The 12 Best Romance Anime On Netflix, Ranked
source_excerpt:
Netflix's romance anime lineup might not be extensive or exhaustive, but it does not lack quality. Whether craving a fluffy get-together, a harem, or a heartbreaking rollercoaster, the subscription service has series that should suit your needs, and many of them rank among the greatest romance anime of all time . The thing is, Netflix lists anime as a genre, so you cannot search for "romance" and "anime" together; consequently, actually finding romance series can be difficult. I hope this article helps simplify matters.
Honestly, romance is probably the most popular genre in anime, in the sense that we are guaranteed to receive at least half a dozen shows each season. Netflix doesn't get most of them, but it usually gets one or two new series, and that includes arguably Fall 2026's best romance anime. Let's go through them.
Updated on October 29, 2026, by Mark Sammut: It's been a while since the last time this article was updated, so I've refreshened everything to make sure the best romance anime on Netflix are accounted for.
Netflix has had a couple of true gems in 2026, and The Ramparts of Ice shines the brightest. Now, I will say that this show is more of a drama that focuses on relationships than a full-blown romance, and you shouldn't go in expecting a traditional arc. Basically, the story revolves around four teenage friends: Koyuki, Minato, Youta, and Miki. Due to awful experiences in middle school, Koyuki keeps everybody but Miki at arm's length; however, that changes when Minato and Youta stumble their way into her life.

The Ramparts of Ice takes a nuanced approach to romance, attraction, and one-sided crushes, exploring the psychological impact they can have on both the person sending and the person receiving the affection. All four characters are incredibly likable and deep, with their backstories adding new dimensions that completely fit their characters while still recontextualizing everything. Very good stuff.
Season 2 is airing as part of the Fall 2026 season .
2 The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity
Simply put, The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity is the best romance anime on Netflix , and you should 100% check it out if you are remotely interested in the genre. Heck, even if you do not love high-school romance, this series might just be an exception. Heartwarming and relatively realistic, Fragrant Flower is about Kaoruko and Rintaro, two teenagers who share a connection despite going to schools that hate each other.
The latter part adds a touch of drama, but Fragrant Flower is mostly happy to let its couple hang out and be cute together. They do not really hide their feelings for each other, even if they tend to manifest in adorably awkward behavior. Some romance anime are stuffed to the brim with drama, while others, like Fragrant Flower, are simply sweet and easy-going.
The Wholesome Romance Anime Between The Best Girl And The Best Boy

One of the most popular anime of the 2020s, My Dress-Up Darling shot up the rankings for one specific reason: Marin. Almost instantly, she set herself up as the definitive "best girl," drawing all the attention. However, what makes the show really work is that Gojou is also kind of the "best boy," and together they are just the "best couple."
For most of his life, Gojou has been a loner, specifically due to his love of making hina dolls, something that most people his age don't really get. In high school, he tries to keep this a secret, but the popular Marin learns the truth and instantly asks him to create costumes for her. From that point on, they are essentially tied at the hip, as they gradually grow closer. My Dress-Up Darling is a brilliant slow-burn romance, and I really mean "slow-burn" in this case. If you absolutely hate shows that refuse to fully bring their characters together, you will hate this anime.
Set primarily in early 20th-century London, the story follows Lili, a Japanese girl who has just enrolled at an art school. To stay in London, she needs to become the academy's top student within half a year, a goal that requires her to overcome an easy-going boy named Kit. These two, naturally, hit it off and serve as the show's main couple. Although not devoid of surprising moments, the romance isn't anything too amazing and is mostly just happy, endearing fluff. Kit is likable enough, but he cannot help but feel like he is just there to be Lili's rival and eventual romantic partner.
Fortunately, Lili is a fantastic female lead, one of the best of 2026 so far. She is passionate, hyper, and ambitious, while also being a bit chaotic and hard-headed. Watching London through her eyes is a constant treat due to her enthusiasm (and the gorgeous animation – Love Through a Prism is stunning). The rest of the recurring characters are also pretty great.
Anime Shows Like Horimiya Kimi ni Todoke
Before 2024, Kimi ni Todoke was great but also somewhat disappointing. After a fantastic 2009 season, the anime dropped a sequel that seemed happy to spin its wheels, refusing to pull the trigger on the core romance until way too late. With no follow-up, this story felt like it never reached its peak.
Fortunately, in 2024, Kimi ni Todoke returned for its third season, which happened to be a Netflix exclusive. These five episodes represent the romance anime genre at its best, telling relatable and mature stories driven by well-defined characters who are constantly learning about themselves. They cover the highs, lows, and insecurities of love, all the while working as coming-of-age character studies.
Just to be clear, newcomers should start from the beginning since Kimi ni Todoke is never anything less than good.
Not Everything Works, But The Main Romance Is Great
One of the more famous Netflix romance anime exclusives, My Happy Marriage has led a strange life. Both seasons debuted to fairly high acclaim, only to fade as they progressed. The show has, admittedly, a few notable weaknesses, specifically a tendency to feature one-note villains. The supernatural element can also come across as half-baked at times, and the action sequences are not great.
For all its flaws, My Happy Marriage gets one thing spot-on: Kiyoka and Miyo's romance. After overcoming some initial uncertainty, these two form a wholesome rapport built on support, tenderness, and honesty. Both characters carry childhood trauma that shaped their outlooks on relationships, and they find solace and love in each other.
An Iconic Comedy With Effective Romance
Rumiko Takahashi's Ranma ½ is one of the most influential and GREAT manga of all time, and it somehow both popularized and subverted the harem genre. The source material received a fantastic adaptation in 1989, but Netflix has the 2024 reboot. Now, Ranma ½ shines primarily as a comedy, as all the characters are over-the-top and hilarious; however, the show can also be enjoyed as a silly romance about two tsunderes who refuse to admit their feelings for each other. They are also stuck in unwanted harems with suitors who can act pretty aggressively.
Although the original anime holds up well (for the most part), the 2024 reboot is shaping up to be the definitive adaptation. The animation is top-notch, and the series modernizes a few elements without ever undermining Ranma ½ 's core appeal. As the manga came to an end a long time ago, the new anime can simply focus on covering the source material, rather than relying on filler.
For people completely unfamiliar with Ranma ½ , the story follows Ranma Saotome , a boy who gender-bends into a girl when he is soaked by water. He is destined to get married to Akane, but they are both very much against the idea.
Your Lie in April is pretty much iconic by this point, and there is a very good chance that anybody remotely interested in romance has already sat through A-1 Pictures' masterful series. For those who haven't, they owe it to themselves to jump into this story, one that is filled with drama, beautiful music, hope, depression, and (polarizing) comedy.
Kosei has not been able to play the piano since his mother's death, but things change when he meets a prodigy named Kaori. This encounter triggers a powerful relationship that goes beyond infatuation or lust, as the two build a strong and unbreakable connection. Impressively, they are not the show's only great characters.
A Sports Romance Anime That Is More Romance Than Sports
Debuting in Fall 2024 , Blue Box offers a rare mix of romance and sports, to the point that fans of both genres should give it a watch. That said, this anime is first and foremost a romance, with the sports aspect being not only secondary but, at times, coming across as irrelevant. Taiki is in love with Chinatsu, the star player of his school's girls' basketball team.
Inspired by her passion for the sport, Taiki decides to take his badminton training seriously, all to ask Chinatsu out after he makes it to nationals. A childhood friend named Hina also has a very obvious crush on Taiki, which just complicates matters.
While not necessarily the most original story, Blue Box nails its characters. All three leads are not only incredibly likable but also have fantastic chemistry with each other, and their banter is quite realistic by the romance genre's standards.
Blue Box season 3 is airing as part of the Fall 2026 season.
An all-time reverse harem classic , Ouran High School Host Club is arguably that genre's ultimate gateway anime. Why? Well, it happens to also be one of the best comedies of all time, while also being a pretty awesome romance (within the confines of a harem structure).
Haruhi, a girl who feels more comfortable dressing up as a male student, ends up joining her school's Host Club to pay off a debt, an agreement that was reached before the club's members realized her gender. Long story short, most of the boys develop feelings for Haruhi, especially the club's president.
Ouran High School Host Club works as well as it does because all the main characters are fully fleshed out, and they are not defined by their relationships with Haruhi. Consequently, any romantic feelings feel completely natural.
